messages:
Evan: Notifying team 19:07 UTC7s ago we observed a peering instability on Iris dedicated (iris-prod <-> onprem-chi). Symptoms: rapid TCP retransmits and short BGP squawks during a large KV checkpoint. Seems similar to other recent peering flaps but with different onprem appliance.
Priya: Which appliance and firmware? Any correlation with maintenance windows?
Evan: Customer says appliance is Palo-Edge v3.2.4, no maintenance window. The event coincides with our checkpoint window at 19:07:12. Packet capture attached to ticket `pcap_2345681234_190712.pcap`.
Noah: I looked at the traces  there's an MTU mismatch warning earlier and a burst of retransmits at 19:07:13-19:07:40. Also saw queue drops on the customer's egress.
Diego: Could be queuing+checkpoint flow saturation. For Nova we implemented a staggered checkpoint hack; worth trying here too.
Iris-Network: We pulled firewall logs: there were bursts of SYN/ACK retransmissions and occasional TCP segmentation. We pushed a temp ACL change at 19:09 but that was reactive.
Priya: Immediate triage proposal: (A) assign remediation lead; (B) enable continuous pcap for the peering pair for next 48h with ring buffer; (C) add a composite alert: (BGP flaps OR retransmit_rate>0.8%) AND checkpoint_active.
Evan: I'll own remediation lead and customer coordination.
Noah: I'll add the pcap hook and extend tcpdump rotation to 200MB chunks. ETA: 12h.
Diego: I'll prototype a KV checkpoint stagger that offsets per-tenant windows by a pseudo-random seed so simultaneous large writes are smoothed. Will have an RFC and test plan in 3 days.
Priya: I'll draft a short customer note: "We're investigating peering instability that surfaces during KV checkpointing. We've engaged remediation and will follow up within 72 hours."
ops-bot: Action: create postmortem issue with label `peering-chain` and add to board `peering-regressions-wg`. Template `postmortem-onprem-v1` applied.
Evan: Recording action items: 1) Evan - remediation lead & customer updates (due 3 business days). 2) Noah - pcap hooks + observability rule (due EOD tomorrow). 3) Diego - staggered checkpoint RFC & sim tests (due 3 days). 4) Priya - customer comms & status notes (due 24h). 5) Priya/Noah - add `kv.checkpoint.*` telemetry fields to peering dashboard for 90 days.
Noah: For alerting I'll add rule: `alert when (bgp_flap OR tcp_retransmit_pct > 0.8) AND kv.checkpoint.active == true` and route to #incidents + oncall.
Diego: Also proposing a medium-term mitigation: adaptive pacing when egress drop > 0.5% for >15s. Will wire into runtime flow-control.
Priya: I'm adding this incident to a recurring-patterns retrospective. Suggest we correlate across Iris, Helix, and Kestrel to see if the same checkpoint cadence overlaps.
Evan: Good call. Add retrospective ticket: `peering-cadence-correlation`. Assign Diego + Noah + Platform SRE.
Iris-Network: We'll provide any additional pcap and syslogs if you need them.
ops-bot: Reminder to attach `pcap_2345681234_190712.pcap` and `bgp_counters_1907.log` to the postmortem issue.
Evan: I'll update the postmortem with timeline, initial hypothesis (egress queue + checkpoint burst), and next steps. WG invite will go out for a triage session tomorrow.
Priya: I'll post the customer-facing update after Evan adds timeline.
Noah: Logging note: enrich peering traces with `kv.checkpoint.size`, `kv.checkpoint.duration_ms`, and `net.egress.drop_pct`. Keep for 90 days.
Diego: I'll run a synthetic test to emulate simultaneous checkpoints across 10 tenants in a staging peered topology next week.
Evan: Thanks team. We'll reconvene after the automated captures collect another event or after the staged test. :thumbsup:
